**1. End-to-End Talent Acquisition**

* Manage the complete recruitment lifecycle, from understanding client requirements to candidate onboarding.
* Handle multiple positions across junior, middle and senior management levels.
* Develop effective sourcing strategies to attract quality candidates.
* Ensure timely closure of open positions as per client expectations and agreed SLAs.

**2. Recruitment Team Management**

* Manage and guide a team of recruiters to achieve individual and collective placement targets.
* Allocate requirements and monitor daily recruitment activities.
* Track recruiter productivity, interview ratios, submission ratios and position closure rates.
* Conduct regular performance reviews and provide coaching to team members.
* Drive accountability, ownership and a performance-oriented recruitment culture.

**3. ATS Management & Recruitment Automation**

* Demonstrate strong expertise in managing and implementing Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).
* Manage job requisitions, candidate databases, recruitment workflows and recruitment dashboards.
* Automate repetitive recruitment activities, including candidate communication, interview scheduling, follow-ups and reporting.
* Optimize ATS utilization to improve recruiter productivity and turnaround time.
* Generate MIS reports and recruitment analytics through ATS and automation tools.
* Explore AI-based recruitment tools for resume screening, sourcing and candidate engagement.

**4. Client & Stakeholder Management**

* Understand client hiring requirements and provide appropriate recruitment solutions.
* Maintain strong relationships with clients and hiring managers.
* Conduct regular follow-ups on interview feedback and selection decisions.
* Ensure a positive candidate and client experience.
* Identify opportunities to improve service delivery and client satisfaction.

**5. Recruitment MIS & Performance Management**

* Prepare and maintain daily, weekly and monthly recruitment MIS.
* Monitor key recruitment metrics:
* Time to Fill
* Time to Hire
* CV Submission Ratio
* Interview-to-Selection Ratio
* Offer-to-Joining Ratio
* Position Closure Rate
* Recruiter Productivity
* Identify bottlenecks and implement corrective measures to improve recruitment performance.

* Graduate in any discipline; MBA/PGDM in HR will be an added advantage.
* Minimum **5 years of experience in Talent Acquisition**, preferably with a recruitment consultancy, staffing or executive search organization.
* Strong experience in end-to-end recruitment and managing multiple client requirements.
* Excellent knowledge of ATS platforms and recruitment automation tools.
* Strong command of Naukri, LinkedIn Recruiter and other sourcing platforms.
* Experience in managing recruitment teams and driving placement targets.
* Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong analytical abilities and proficiency in MS Excel and recruitment MIS.
* Ability to work in a target-driven and deadline-oriented environment.

Preferred Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate should be:

* Technology-oriented and passionate about recruitment automation.
* A hands-on recruitment professional with strong sourcing and closure capabilities.
* Capable of independently managing recruitment delivery and a team of recruiters.
* Data-driven, process-oriented and focused on improving recruitment productivity.
* Comfortable working in a fast-paced recruitment consulting environment.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Performance will be measured on:

* Monthly placement and position closure targets.
* Timely fulfilment of client requirements.
* Recruiter productivity and team performance.
* ATS adoption and effective utilization.
* Recruitment automation and process improvements.
* Quality of hiring and candidate joining ratio.
* Client satisfaction and retention.

* Opportunity to lead and improve recruitment operations.
* Exposure to technology-driven recruitment and automation.
* Ownership of recruitment delivery and team performance.
* Opportunity to grow with an expanding HR and recruitment solutions organization.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Security Platform: Authentication
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100\* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.*

**An overview of this role**
----------------------------

As a Staff Software Engineer on GitLab's Authentication team, you'll be the technical lead for how every user, application, token, and automated agent proves who it is on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.

We're an OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for millions of users. We also accept identity from enterprise identity providers through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) and Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP). Behind that sit more than ten token types and several session methods that grew inside the Ruby on Rails monolith. You'll help us move this work onto GATE, GitLab's new authentication and authorization platform. GATE exchanges external credentials for short-lived tokens at the edge through a Secure Token Service written in Go.You'll set our technical direction, lead the hardest protocol and migration work yourself, and help senior engineers own the rest.

Our projects include:

* **OAuth across Cells:** Making OAuth clients, grants, and tokens work when users and organizations live in different cells
* **Global identities:** One user identity that works across organizations and cells
* **Token consolidation:** Reducing the number of token types and moving token issuance and validation out of the monolith
* **Identity for artificial intelligence (AI) agents and workloads:** OAuth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients, workload identity federation, and service identities with narrow scopes

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Own the technical direction for authentication protocols at GitLab, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and token exchange, across the Rails monolith and GATE services.
* Write and drive design documents and architecture decision records (ADRs) for multi-quarter work, then break that work into increments that ship behind feature flags.
* Lead migrations that must not break existing customers: token formats, client and grant state, and session behavior on GitLab.com, Self-Managed, and Dedicated.
* Be hands-on in the most complex parts of the code, in Ruby on Rails and Go, and review the designs and merge requests of other engineers.
* Agree interface contracts with the GATE Core, GATE Infra, Authorization, and Tenant Scale (Cells and Organizations) teams, and keep them current as the architecture changes.
* Treat authentication as a security and availability boundary: threat-model new flows, add rate limits and abuse controls, and lead the technical response to authentication incidents.
* Mentor senior and intermediate engineers on the team and raise the protocol and security knowledge of the whole group.
* Work asynchronously with engineers in India, Europe, and the Americas, with most decisions made in writing.
* Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

**What you'll bring**
---------------------

* Significant experience building and running production authentication or identity systems at scale, with technical leadership across teams that moves unclear problems to written decisions and shipped code.
* Deep, hands-on knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC: authorization code with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE), refresh token rotation, token exchange, client registration, scopes, and JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) with signing keys and key rotation.
* Working knowledge of SAML 2.0 single sign-on and enterprise identity integration (LDAP, System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM), or similar).
* Strong production experience in Ruby on Rails or Go, willingness to work in both, and experience with careful refactors, feature-flagged rollouts, and backward-compatible migrations in large, long-lived codebases.
* A security mindset. You think about token theft, replay, revocation, and blast radius before you think about elegance.
* Experience with multi-tenant software as a service (SaaS) systems, including data isolation and performance under high request volume.
* Clear, concise written English and comfort working in an all-remote, asynchronous company.
* Optional experience: authentication libraries (Doorkeeper, Devise, or OmniAuth), passkeys or multi-factor authentication, workload identity, gateways or policy engines, AI agent authentication, or multi-region architectures. Contributions to identity standards or open source identity projects are also welcome.

**About the team**
------------------

The Authentication group is part of the Security Platform stage, alongside Authorization, GATE Core, GATE Infra, Secrets Manager, and other security teams. We own sign-in, single sign-on, OAuth, and personal and service tokens. Our work touches every GitLab customer, and much of it is on the critical path for Cells and for GitLab's AI agent platform.

* Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
* Flexible Paid Time Off
* Team Member Resource Groups
* Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Growth and Development Fund
* Parental Leave

title: Director – People & Operations
company: iForest - International Forum for Environment, Sustainability & Technology
description:
Reference code: DO/NCR-11/26

The International Forum for Environment, Sustainability & Technology (iFOREST) is looking for an experienced and dynamic leader to build and head the organisation’s people and operations functions, covering HR, administration and IT, across its three offices.

A successful applicant must have a proven record of leading HR functions, building HR policies, systems and teams in a growing organisation, and advising senior leadership on organisation design and workforce planning, and good communication skills with researchers, managers, and external agencies. The candidate should ideally have work experience in a think tank, non-profit or international NGO.

#### **Position summary**

**Title**

Director – People & Operations

  

**Reports to**

Chief Executive Officer

  

**Direct reports**

Manager – Culture & People; Manager – Talent Aquisiton, Manager – Operations

  

**Location**

Noida head office

  

**Experience**

20+ years in HR, with significant exposure to administration, including at least 10 years leading a function

  

**Remuneration**

Depending upon qualification and experience

#### **About iFOREST**

iFOREST is an independent, not-for-profit research and innovation organisation established in 2019. It identifies, promotes and scales up solutions for pressing environment–development challenges in India and other developing countries in Asia and Africa.

Our work is rooted in regional priorities. We accelerate environmental action at the sub-national level and use that regional knowledge to improve national policies and plans and strengthen international collaboration. We conduct independent, evidence-based research, develop new knowledge and innovative solutions, convene stakeholders to build consensus, and partner with think tanks, civil society, government agencies, philanthropies and industry to scale up solutions.

Much of our work is funded by international grants and delivered with state and district partners. We have a team of about 80 people across three offices in India.

#### **Purpose of the role**

The Director – People & Operations will build and lead iFOREST’s HR and administration support functions. HR is the primary focus of the role. The Director is a member of the senior management team and a close adviser to the CEO.

iFOREST is a young organisation, and many of its policies, SOPs and systems are evolving. A key aim is to take day-to-day HR and administrative work off the senior management, so they can focus on research, programmes and partnerships.

Success in this role means that, within a year:

* iFOREST has an approved, legally compliant and implementable set of HR and administrative policies, SOPs and delegations that staff understand, and managers apply consistently.
* Hiring keeps pace with new grants, and the organisation attracts and retains strong research and programme staff.
* Staff costs, contracts, records and procurement meet the requirements of donors and auditors without last-minute effort.
* The CEO is no longer involved in routine HR and administrative decisions.

#### **Key responsibilities**

Roughly 70% of the role is HR, and 30% is administration and IT oversight.

#### **1. HR and Administration leadership**

* Lead, coach and develop the HR and administration Team, setting clear goals and standards of service.
* Build a service culture in which staff in every office know whom to contact and get timely answers.

#### **2. Strategy, policy and organisation design**

* Develop a people and operations strategy aligned with iFOREST’s mission, growth plans and values, in consultation with the CEO and senior management.
* Write, obtain approval for and ensure roll out the HR manual, administration manual, IT policy and the SOPs that sit under them, in line with good practice and applicable law.
* Propose a delegation of financial and administrative authority.
* Advise the CEO and senior management on organisation design, role levels, grading, spans of control and workforce planning.
* Prepare and manage the annual budget for HR, administration and IT, and track spending against it.

#### **5. Talent acquisition and onboarding**

* Plan staffing with programme heads for ongoing and new grants, including staffing assumptions for proposals.
* Lead recruitment at all levels: senior leadership, researchers, programme and field staff, fellows, interns, consultants and support staff.
* Set up fair, documented hiring processes, from job descriptions and sourcing to interview panels, reference checks and offers.
* Build iFOREST’s employer brand with universities, professional networks and peer institutions.
* Run structured onboarding and induction, including for staff joining regional offices.

#### **6. Performance, learning and careers**

* Run the annual performance cycle, including goal setting, probation reviews and feedback.
* Develop role levels, competencies, promotion criteria and career paths.
* Identify learning needs and lead training, mentoring and capacity building.
* Support leadership development and succession planning for critical roles.

#### **7. Compensation, benefits, payroll and grant compliance**

* Maintain a salary structure and benefits that are competitive in the think-tank and development sector, and administer leave and other benefits as per the company policies.
* Coordinate monthly payroll inputs and statutory deductions with the Finance team to ensure accuracy and timeliness.
* Work with Finance and programme teams on charging staff costs to grants, timesheets and effort reporting, and donor rules on salaries, consultants and benefits.
* Respond to the HR and administration sections of donor due-diligence reviews and audits.

#### **8. Employee relations, safeguarding and compliance**

* Develop, review, and update the HR manual, administrative manuals, guidelines, and SOPs in line with industry best practices and applicable laws.
* Ensure compliance with Indian labour and employment laws across all three offices, including state-specific registrations and returns.
* Ensure compliance with the POSH Act, including a functioning Internal Committee, awareness sessions and annual reporting.
* Develop and run a safeguarding policy and code of conduct that meets the expectations of iFOREST’s international donors, covering staff, consultants and partners working in communities.
* Oversee employment contracts, consultant and fellowship agreements, vendor service level agreements (SLAs), and official institutional documentation.
* Manage grievances, disciplinary matters and exits fairly, consistently and confidentially, including full-and-final settlements and analysis of attrition.
* Ensure personal data of staff is held securely and in line with data protection law.

#### **9. Culture, engagement and inclusion**

* Build an open, collaborative and mission-driven culture across head office and regional offices.
* Promote diversity, equity and inclusion in hiring, pay and progression.
* Lead staff wellbeing and duty of care, especially for field and regional staff who travel.

#### **10. Administration and facilities**

* Oversee office management, facilities, security and maintenance at head office and regional offices.
* Set up procurement and vendor management that is cost-effective and meets donor procurement rules.
* Oversee asset registers, insurance and annual physical verification.
* Oversee travel, logistics, events and support for workshops and visiting delegations, including visas and protocol for international guests.
* Oversee health, safety and business continuity plans for all offices.
* Make sure the CEO and senior management receive reliable administrative support, so they are freed from day-to-day administrative matters.

#### **11. IT and digital systems**

* Set direction for IT infrastructure, user support, information security and backups across all offices.
* Oversee selection and roll-out of HR, payroll and administrative systems (HRMS and MIS).
* Ensure IT policies, licences and data handling meet donor and legal requirements.
  

#### **Key relationships and authority**

**Relationship**

**Nature of work**

**CEO**

Reports to; adviser on people, organisation and operations matters

  

**Senior management and programme heads**

Partner on workforce planning, hiring, performance and team issues

  

**Finance**

Partner on payroll, budgets, staff-cost allocation to grants, procurement, audits

  

**Grants and programme teams**

Staffing in proposals, donor HR and procurement clauses, due diligence

  

**Regional office leads**

Delivery of HR, administration and IT services in each office

  

**Board or its committees**

Reports on people matters, policies and compliance as required

  

**External**

Legal and statutory advisers, auditors, insurers, recruitment partners, vendors, labour authorities

The Director will have authority, within approved policies, budgets and the delegation of authority, to approve routine HR, administrative and IT decisions.

#### **Qualifications and experience**

**Essential**

* Master’s degree in human resource management, personnel management, business or public administration, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
* 20+ years of progressive HR experience, with significant responsibility for administration, including at least 10 years leading an HR or operations function.
* End-to-end experience across recruitment, performance management, compensation and benefits, employee relations and compliance.
* Experience managing staff and services across more than one location.
* Experience building HR policies, systems and processes in a new or fast-growing organisation.
* Working knowledge of Indian labour laws and the POSH Act.

**Desirable**

* Experience in a think tank, research institution, non-profit, development organisation or international NGO.
* Experience with internationally funded grants, including donor rules on staff costs, procurement and safeguarding.
* Experience overseeing administration, procurement or IT functions.
* Experience introducing an HRMS or similar digital system.

**Competencies**

* Ability to turn organisational goals into practical people and operations plans.
* Writes clear policies and SOPs and gets them adopted.
* Builds trust with senior researchers, programme leaders and staff at all levels.
* Handles confidential and sensitive matters with integrity and discretion.
* Makes fair, consistent judgements in employee relations.
* Delegates well and develops a team, rather than doing the team’s work.
* Communicates clearly in English, in writing and in person.

#### **What we offer**

iFOREST provides an inclusive and supportive work environment and is committed to professional development through education, training and capacity building. We offer salaries that are competitive in the think-tank sector and recognise performance through annual appraisals.

Remuneration: Depending on qualifications and experience. The final designation will depend on the selected candidate’s qualifications and experience.

#### **How to apply**

Apply online at iforest.global/careers. If you have difficulty applying online, send your CV and a cover letter to careers@iforest.global with “Director – People & Operations” in the subject line.

Immediate opening. The position is open until filled.

Published

Nov 11, 2026

You may also apply by writing to careers@iforest.global with the position and
  
reference code in subject line.

#### **Why Choose iFOREST**

* Purpose-driven work: Contribute from regional to national and global goals in
    
  sustainability.
* Professional development: Work in areas that address contemporary and critical issues.
* Competitive compensation: We recognize and reward commitment and talent.
* Inclusive culture: Experience a supportive, diverse, and empowering work environment.

FHI 360 serves more than 60 countries and all U.S. states and territories.

***Job Summary:***

The Technical Director – HIV will provide overall technical leadership and direction for FHI 360’s HIV/AIDS technical assistance activities in India. Headquartered in New Delhi, India, the Technical Director will lead the planning, implementation, and technical oversight of activities designed to strengthen HIV case finding, reducing AIDS-related deaths, eliminating vertical transmission and sustaining epidemic control, along with integration with other health priorities. Working under the leadership of the AFGHS Project Director, the Technical Director – HIV will have primary responsibility for ensuring the technical quality and effective implementation of FHI 360’s HIV/AIDS portfolio, including oversight and mentoring of HIV technical personnel and consultants and coordination of technical activities, work plans, and associated budgets. The Technical Director - HIV will lead the development and implementation of annual and activity-specific work plans, monitor progress against established objectives and deliverables, identify and address implementation challenges, and ensure activities are completed on schedule and within approved budgets.

The Technical Director – HIV will serve as a principal technical liaison for FHI 360’s HIV activities with the National AIDS Control Organization (NACO) under the Government of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the U.S. Department of State partners, and other organizations supporting HIV/AIDS technical assistance in India. The Technical Director -HIV will promote strong coordination and alignment with government priorities and partner activities while identifying opportunities to leverage and integrate FHI 360’s broader health programming and technical capabilities. The position will support assessments, capacity strengthening, and technical assistance to national and subnational counterparts; provide oversight for high-quality technical, programmatic, and financial reporting; and ensure that FHI 360’s HIV activities are evidence-based, responsive to identified epidemiological and programmatic gaps, and implemented in accordance with donor requirements, FHI 360 policies, and national priorities.

***Accountabilities:***

The Technical Director-HIV works in close collaboration with the FHI 360 headquarters (HQ) technical team, planning and directing technical strategies and implementation of projects. S/he will lead the country HIV project team in the planning of project activities until completion of the project.

* Support rapid start-up of HIV activities in country, in alignment with donor and NACP priorities.
* Provide technical leadership to the HIV country team and liaise with AFGHS-HIV leadership at the global level to define, develop, implement, monitor and adjust technical work plans, presentations, and reports.
* Provide technical leadership in liaising with NACO, State AIDS Control Societies (SACS), and other relevant national and sub-national institutions in achieving project priorities through above-site and catalytic technical assistance.
* Ensure alignment of the HIV technical assistance priorities through annual work planning based on NACP priorities, epidemiological and programmatic evidence, transition needs, and available resources.
* Actively support in implementation oversight, performance monitoring and technical quality of HIV services as prioritized in the approved AFGHS workplan.
* Support national policy development, program optimization, performance monitoring, and quality improvement initiatives as planned under NACP and AFGHS Project.
* Contribute towards epidemic control preparedness, health system coordination, and multistakeholder collaboration across government departments, development partners, and civil society.

* Provide HIV care and treatment related technical and management support to HIV facilities and implementing partners under NACP to strengthen case management services, ensure ART initiation and strengthen viral load suppression through innovative, evidence-based programming.
* Remain informed on current state-of-the-art technical updates in HIV care and treatment through review of literature and articles and maintains link with other international bodies which specialize in at-risk population focused HIV treatment care and support.
* Ensure that the project technical deliverables meet or exceed quality standards. Ensure on-time delivery of high-quality deliverables and reports.
* Responsible for onboarding project staff and ensuring their familiarity with organizational and project mandate, values, quality standards, policies and objectives and their individual responsibilities in upholding these standards and policies.
* Support performance management and professional development of direct reports, including ongoing feedback, coaching, and career support.
* Ensure financial and contractual compliance with FHI 360 and donor rules and regulations.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Project Director, or as requested from the leadership of the national program.

* MBBS degree and master’s degree in public health, epidemiology and other related areas would be an added advantage.

* Demonstrated experience in managing and leading teams of donor-funded projects.
* Experience working collaboratively with government institutions (especially NACO and SACS), INGOs, and multilateral organizations.
* Highly proficient with MS Project, and the Microsoft suite of programs (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Visio).
* Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
* Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills.

title: Lead Specialist - Learning and Development
description:
**Introduction**  

Welcome to Gallagher in India — where expertise, technology, and purpose come together. Since 2006, Gallagher in India has supported global teams by delivering quality, service, and speed through deep expertise, smart technology, and specialized knowledge services. More than just an operations center, it’s a place where careers grow through collaboration, continuous learning, and purposeful work. We drive efficiency, compliance, and innovation so our teams can focus on serving clients. If you enjoy solving problems and working with purpose, Gallagher is the place where you can grow and feel a sense of belonging.

  
**Overview**

The Program Manager Role at Gallagher Company will be responsible for managing the end-to-end administrative activities associated with certain programs. This role balances between Program Design and Administration of the Learning Program.

  
  
**How you'll make an impact**

**Responsibilities:**

  

* Program Planning:
* Program Preparation:
* Finalize Roster and Update Resources/Teams:
* Creation of Cohort Training Schedules:
* Graduation Certificates
* Creation of Invites
* Program Communications:
* Program Resources:
* Participant Tracking:
* State License Tracking:
* Onboarding Curriculum Creation
* Revenue Reporting
* Training Desktop Set-up for Workflow Training
* SharePoint Calendar Management
* Case Study Auditing
* Survey Creation, Analysis and Dashboard creation for Programs

**Key Activities:**

* Create key dates for each class, 6 months to 1 year in advance of the program start date.
* Gain agreement from Program Leader and VP of Emerging Talent, then share with TA (Talent Acquisition).
* Create/update master plan spreadsheet for new classes, including key dates to populate formulas.
* Build the program plan in MS Teams Planner and assign tasks.
* Partner with TA and ARCs (Achieve Regional Coordinators) to confirm the final class roster.
* Pull reports from Talent Connect; review Oracle reports and add approved/pending review employees from the Waitlist tab on the master tracker.
* Email ARCs with a deadline to review/confirm the roster and make necessary changes.
* Update Leader Contact List after Learning Coach assignments are confirmed.
* Create private channel for the new class in MS Teams and add participants.
* Create training cohort schedules.
* Creation, shipping and inventory management of graduation certificates and coordination with vendors on the shipping. Coordination with class and vendor to ship graduation pullovers.
* Create all Invites for Kickoffs and other scheduled trainings, The calendar owner will need to add the Teams meeting and send the invite.
* Manage ARC/Participant communications and MS Teams posts.
* Maintain Participant Travel Guidelines document for Trusted Partner.
* Maintain Travel Form for scheduling and in-person purposes.
* Maintain high-level Overview resource and support updating other resources.
* Prepare the requests for SIT code changes and title changes as needed throughout the program for each class.
* Update Master Tracker with new classes, training dates, manager changes, and program status changes.
* Create tracking form for state license tracking and share progress reports with program Leadership.
* Create curriculums and class group for each class. Assign each curriculum according to designated schedule. Run progress reports and send to Program Leadership based on established timelines.
* Complete participant set-up in the Training Desktop for Workflow Training based on instructions provided.
* Maintain schedule for revenue reporting as new classes are added and run reports for Program Leadership based on this schedule.
* Update all trainings and key dates on the SharePoint Calendar for each class

  
  
**About you**

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Human Resources or related field is preferred.
* Minimum of 8-10 years of experience as Program manager/ training coordinator or operations specialist
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data and provide actionable insights.
* Strong organizational and time management skills.
* Attention to detail and ability to manage multiple initiatives simultaneously.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build relationships and influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
* Proficiency in MS Office suite (Especially Excel), MS Projects, Jira or MS Planner is preferred.

At Gallagher, we believe supporting our colleagues goes far beyond the role itself. For more information, visit our Benefits page.

* Competitive compensation

* Career development opportunities and ongoing learning
* A collaborative, people-first culture with accessible leadership
* The opportunity to do meaningful work with global reach and local impact

**At Gallagher, we are dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace.** If your past experience doesn’t align perfectly, we encourage you to join our Talent Community to stay connected to additional career opportunities. At times, we will consider transferable skills from previous roles.

title: Plant HR & Admin Manager
description:
**HR & Admin Manager – Manufacturing Plant**

**Department:** Human Resources & Administration  
**Location:** Shadnagar, Telangana  
**Reporting To:** Plant Manager  
**Salary:** ₹30,000 – ₹70,000 per month  
**Employment Type:** Full-time, Work from Office

Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced HR & Admin Manager to independently manage the entire Human Resources and Administration function at our manufacturing plant in Shadnagar.

The role involves managing manpower planning and recruitment, HR operations, payroll, time office, employee and industrial relations, statutory compliance, contract labour management, training and development, and overall plant administration. The candidate will be responsible for ensuring workforce availability, employee welfare, statutory compliance, workplace discipline and smooth administrative operations.

Key Responsibilities

**1. Manpower Planning & Recruitment**

* Manage annual manpower budgeting, workforce planning and deployment.
* Handle end-to-end recruitment of blue-collar workers, staff, trainees and apprentices.
* Manage recruitment consultants, job portals and campus hiring.
* Oversee offer management, joining formalities, onboarding and induction.
* Maintain recruitment trackers and MIS.

**2. HR Operations**

* Manage the complete employee lifecycle, including confirmation, transfers, promotions and separations.
* Maintain employee records, documentation, HR letters and certificates.
* Implement HR policies, procedures and SOPs.
* Oversee HRMS administration and employee documentation.

**3. Payroll & Time Office**

* Oversee payroll processing, attendance verification and salary coordination.
* Manage biometric attendance, leave administration and shift scheduling.
* Monitor overtime, incentives, shift allowances and other payroll components.
* Handle loan recoveries, Full & Final settlements and Income Tax coordination.
* Ensure accurate attendance records and timely payroll processing.

**4. Performance Management**

* Implement KRAs, KPIs and performance management systems.
* Coordinate confirmation reviews, mid-year and annual appraisals.
* Manage increment processes and performance tracking.
* Prepare performance management reports.

**5. Training & Development**

* Conduct Training Need Analysis and prepare annual training calendars.
* Coordinate technical, behavioural and safety training.
* Facilitate skill development and leadership development programmes.
* Maintain employee skill matrices and training records.

**6. Employee & Industrial Relations**

* Handle employee grievances, counselling and disciplinary matters.
* Conduct domestic enquiries and manage disciplinary proceedings.
* Maintain harmonious industrial relations with employees, workmen and contractors.
* Drive employee engagement, recognition and welfare initiatives.
* Facilitate worker communication and resolve workplace issues.

**7. Labour Law & Statutory Compliance**

* Ensure compliance with applicable labour laws, including Factory Act, EPF, ESIC, Bonus, Gratuity, Minimum Wages, Contract Labour regulations, Labour Welfare Fund and Professional Tax.
* Maintain statutory registers, records, returns and documentation.
* Coordinate statutory inspections, compliance audits and government liaison.
* Ensure compliance with contractor-related statutory requirements and applicable labour regulations.

**8. Contract Labour Management**

* Manage contractor onboarding, manpower deployment and coordination.
* Verify contract labour attendance, wage payments and statutory documentation.
* Monitor contractor licences, registrations and compliance.
* Verify contractor bills and manpower deployment.
* Coordinate with production teams to ensure adequate workforce availability.

**9. Plant Administration**

* Manage overall plant administration and facilities.
* Supervise security, housekeeping, gardening, canteen, guest house and transport.
* Manage visitor entry, access control and security arrangements.
* Oversee uniforms, PPE, employee amenities and welfare facilities.
* Coordinate facility maintenance, asset management and administrative vendors.
* Monitor administrative budgets, vendor contracts and service quality.

**10. HR MIS, Budgeting & Digitalisation**

* Prepare and review monthly HR and Administration MIS.
* Monitor absenteeism, attrition, overtime, manpower costs and workforce productivity.
* Prepare annual HR and Administration budgets and track expenditure.
* Drive implementation and effective utilisation of HRMS, ATS, PMS, payroll and attendance systems.
* Develop HR dashboards, reporting systems and process improvements.

**11. Coordination & Operational Support**

* Work closely with the Plant Manager, Production, Finance, EHS and other departments.
* Ensure adequate manpower availability for uninterrupted plant operations.
* Support workplace safety, employee welfare and operational discipline.
* Identify process gaps and implement improvements in HR and administrative operations.

**Educational Qualification**

* MBA / PGDM in Human Resources or Personnel Management.
* Postgraduate qualification in Labour Welfare or Industrial Relations will be an added advantage.

**Experience**

* 10–15 years of overall HR experience, preferably in a manufacturing or industrial environment.
* Strong experience in plant HR, blue-collar recruitment, labour law compliance, industrial relations and contract labour management.
* Experience independently managing plant administration and large workforces.
* Experience coordinating payroll, time office and statutory compliance.

**Required Skills & Competencies**

* Strong knowledge of labour laws and statutory compliance.
* Excellent employee relations, industrial relations and conflict-resolution skills.
* Strong leadership and team management abilities.
* Good communication, negotiation and problem-solving skills.
* Proficiency in MS Excel, HRMS, payroll systems and HR reporting.
* Ability to independently manage HR and administrative operations at a manufacturing plant.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**

* Timely fulfilment of manpower requirements.
* Statutory compliance and audit performance.
* Payroll and attendance accuracy.
* Absenteeism, attrition and manpower cost control.
* Contractor compliance and documentation accuracy.
* Grievance resolution and industrial relations.
* Training effectiveness and employee engagement.
* Administrative cost optimisation and facility management.

**Overall Accountability:** To independently manage the complete HR and Administration function of the plant, ensuring a disciplined, compliant, productive and employee-focused workplace while supporting uninterrupted manufacturing operations.
